ITQAN:v4p347/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p347/r4.speaker: جعفر بن شمس الخلافة
ITQAN:v4p347/r4.claim: Ja'far lists this Qur'anic clause among expressions used proverbially (irsāl al-mathal).
ITQAN:v4p347/r4.anchor: عقد جعفر بن شمس الخلافة في كتاب الآداب بابا في ألفاظ من القرآن جارية مجرى المثل

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.speaker: أبي بن خلف
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from al-Sadiq that Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbled a decayed bone and challenged the resurrection; God answered that the one who first created it will revive it.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال جاء أبي بن خلف فأخذ عظما باليا من حائط ففته

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعروة بن الزبير وقتادة والسدي وعكرمة
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur gives many routes for a similar report, while other reports from Ibn Abbas name al-As ibn Wa'il or Abd Allah ibn Ubayy as the challenger.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.anchor: وروى مثله في الدر المنثور بطرق كثيرة عن ابن عباس وعروة بن الزبير وعن قتادة والسدي وعكرمة

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.claim: Al-Tabataba'i notes the alternate attributions of the bone challenge to al-As ibn Wa'il and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy in other Ibn Abbas reports.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.anchor: وروى أيضا عن ابن عباس أن القائل هو العاص بن وائل وبطريق آخر عنه أن القائل هو عبد الله بن أبي

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.claim: The one who originated a person from nothing and without a prior model can restore that person as originally created.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.anchor:
قال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" إن الذي أنشأه من غير شيء وصوره على غير مثال كان سبق إليه قادر أن يعيده كما بدأه

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.claim: Souls remain in their stations; bodily remains are preserved in earth and reassembled after the resurrection rain, then reunited with each soul.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.anchor: إن الروح مقيمة في مكانها روح المحسن في ضياء وفسحة، وروح المسيء في ضيق وظلمة

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.speaker: نهج البلاغة
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.claim: God's creative command is an effective act, not an audible sound; if it were eternal, that would imply a second deity.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.anchor: لما أراد كونه كن فيكون، لا بصوت يقرع ولا نداء يسمع وإنما كلامه سبحانه فعل منه أنشأه

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.claim: Safwan reports that human will is inward intention followed by action, while God's will is simply bringing something into existence.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.anchor: الإرادة من الخلق الضمير وما يبدو لهم بعد ذلك من الفعل، وأما من الله فإرادته إحداثه لا غير ذلك

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.claim: The Imams' reports are numerous in treating divine will as an attribute of action rather than an inward creaturely state.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.anchor: والروايات عنهم عليه السلام في كون إرادته من صفات الفعل مستفيضة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.claim: The closing section resumes the opening themes of monotheism and the Hereafter and assures the Prophet that he awakens the morally living, not the dead-hearted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.anchor: what was discussed in the opening one is take up again in a different style

STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.claim: These verses voice a common objection to the Qur'anic teaching of bodily resurrection, also raised elsewhere in the Qur'an.
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.anchor: These verses express a common objection to the Quranic understanding of bodily resurrection (cf. 13:5; 17:49, 98; 23:35, 82–83; 27:67;

STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.speaker: IK, JJ, Q, W
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet withered bones, crushed them, and challenged their revival; the Prophet affirmed it and warned that Ubayy would be cast into the Fire, after which these verses were revealed.
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.anchor: it is reported that a man by the name of Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought some withered bones to the Prophet and crushed them into pieces

STUDYQURAN:36:78/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r3.claim: The phrase can also be rendered “having forgotten his own creation.”
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r3.anchor: And forgotten his own creation could also be rendered “having forgotten his own creation.”

BURSEVI:v7p341/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p341/r3.claim: The human's surprising quarrel is followed by his strange assertion that God cannot revive bones, an extraordinary and irrational denial of God's power over a possible thing.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r3.anchor: أورد في شأننا قصة عجيبة في نفس الأمر وهي في الغرابة والبعد عن العقول كالمثل

BURSEVI:v7p341/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r4.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v7p341/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says mathal is borrowed for a strange event, likened in its oddity to a familiar proverbial saying.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r4.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ المثل يستعار للأمر العجيب تشبيها له في الغرابة بالمثل العرفي الذي هو القول السائر

BURSEVI:v7p341/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p341/r5.claim: Forgetting his creation means forgetting that God made him from a drop; reflection on this beginning would show that resurrection is no different, since both bring inert matter to life.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r5.anchor: والمصدر مضاف إلى المفعول أي : خلقنا إياه من النطفة

BURSEVI:v7p341/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r6.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v7p341/r6.claim: Al-Baqli says the two worlds are gathered in the human; knowing oneself is knowing one's Lord, for the creature is a mirror of reality in which divine reality appears to knowers, and God revives the ignorant heart.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r6.anchor: لأن الكونين والعالمين في الإنسان مجموعون وفيه علمه معلوم لو عرف نفسه فقد عرف ربه لأن الخليقة مرآة الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v7p341/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p341/r7.claim: The denier asks who could revive the bones, stressing that they have decayed completely, with no skin, flesh, veins, or nerves remaining.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r7.anchor: منكرا له أشد النكير مؤكدا له بقوله

BURSEVI:v7p341/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p341/r8.claim: Ramim means badly decayed; the root is ramma-yarimm with rimma, and the word is a substantive for decayed bones rather than an adjective, explaining why it is not feminine.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r8.anchor: يقال رم العظم يرم رمة بكسر الراء فيهما أي : بلى فهو رميم

BURSEVI:v7p342/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p342/r1.claim: Shafiʿi, Malik, and Ahmad infer from the verse that bones are living and a dead person's bones are impure; Hanafis treat bones like hair and understand reviving them as restoring softness and moisture in a living, sensitive body.
BURSEVI:v7p342/r1.anchor: وقد تمسك بظاهر الآية الكريمة من أثبت للعظم حياة وبنى عليه الحكم بنجاسة عظم الميت وهو الشافعي ومالك وأحمد

BURSEVI:v7p342/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v7p342/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa says a human becomes impure at death because he has blood, but is purified by washing as an honor; prayer for him in a mosque is disliked.
BURSEVI:v7p342/r2.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : يتنجس لأنه دموي إلا أنه يطهر بالغسل كرامة له وتكره الصلاة عليه في المسجد

BURSEVI:v7p342/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342/r3.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد
BURSEVI:v7p342/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad say a human is not made impure by death and prayer in a mosque is not disliked; Malik has differing reports, with purity the stronger view and mosque prayer disliked in his well-known position.
BURSEVI:v7p342/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأحمد لا يتنجس به ولا تكره الصلاة عليه فيه وعن مالك خلاف والأظهر الطهارة

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the questioner who brought a bone to the Prophet as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} [يس: 78] قال: «أبي بن خلف أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r2.claim: Mujahid specifically identifies the person who made the parable as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وضرب لنا مثلا} [يس: 78] «أبي بن خلف»

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r3.claim: Qatada reports that Ubayy crushed a dry bone and scattered it in the wind, challenged the Prophet, heard that God would revive it and then send him to Hell, and was later killed at Uhud.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} [يس: 78] ذكر لنا أن أبي بن خلف، أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم حائل

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies the questioner as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who crumbled a dry bone and asked whether God would raise it; the Prophet answered yes, and the verses were revealed.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: جاء العاص بن وائل السهمي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم حائل، ففته بين يديه، فقال: يا محمد أيبعث الله هذا حيا بعدما أرم؟

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the questioner as ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who broke a dry bone and asked how God could raise it; the response says God will revive it and send him to Hell.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه، من نطفة} [يس: 77] . . إلى قوله: {وهي رميم} [يس: 78] قال: جاء عبد الله بن أبي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.claim: The person who doubts resurrection forgets that God created him from a drop, then made him a fully formed disputant who argues against his Lord’s promise to revive the dead.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.anchor: فتأويل الكلام إذن: أولم ير هذا الإنسان الذي يقول: {من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} [يس: 78] أنا خلقناه من نطفة فسويناه خلقا سويا {فإذا هو خصيم} [يس: 77] يقول: فإذا هو ذو خصومة لربه، يخاصمه فيما قال له ربه

TAB-FULL:v19p488/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r1.claim: The denier likened God to created beings unable to revive decayed bones, forgetting that God first created him.
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r1.anchor: لا يعجز أن يعيد الأموات أحياء، والعظام الرميم بشرا

TAB-FULL:v19p488/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r2.claim: The man forgot God made him from a drop into a complete, articulate human; the Creator who originated him can restore the dead to their former form.
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r2.anchor: من خلقه من نطفة حتى صار بشرا سويا ناطقا

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r7.claim: رميم means bones that have decayed.

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r8.claim: The phrase نسي خلقه is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ضرب.
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r8.anchor: { نسي خلقه } حال من فاعل ضرب

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r9.claim: The question about who revives the bones explains the example he posed; it is unjoined because it means, in effect, What example did he pose? He said: who revives them?
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r9.anchor: بيان للمثل الذي ضربه الإنسان، ولذلك جيء به مفصولا من غير عطف

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.claim: The challenger forgets his first creation from a sperm drop; if he remembered it, he could answer his own challenge by recalling that initial creation, as God instructs the Prophet to do.
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.anchor: وضرب الإنسان لنا مثلا وقد نسي خلقه من نطفة لأول مرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r1.claim: Muqatil says the man made a likeness by crumbling and scattering a decayed bone to deny resurrection and mock anyone saying God would revive it; his challenge is effectively to revive that bone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬4): وصف لنا شبها، يعني: أنه ضرب المثل في إنكار البعث بالعظم الحائل، ففته وبذره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r2.claim: Muqatil says he forgot to consider his own creation: he was made from a drop after previously being nothing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ونسي خلقه}. قال مقاتل: يقول: وترك النظر في خلق نفسه ءأذا خلق من نطفة ولم يك قبل ذلك شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd says ramīm is like rimma; the bone crumbles and is described as decayed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: الرميم مثل الرمة، يقال منه: رم العظم، وهو يرم رما، وهو رميم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r4.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi says the bones have decayed when they are described as رمّت or أرمت.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: رمت عظامه وأرمت إذا بليت (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses ramīm as fragments or dust.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r6.claim: Ramīm lacks a feminine ending despite describing bones because it is transferred from an active participle; as it is not formed as a verb-derived adjective here, it takes no feminine marker.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p526/r6.anchor: وإنما قال رميم بغير هاء، وهو صفة العظام؛ لأنه منقول عن فاعل، فهو غير مبني على الفعل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r7.claim: The denier asks how God can revive great, crumbled bones but forgets his own first creation; remembering it would have kept him from denying resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r7.anchor: ونسي ابتداء خلقه؛ لأنه لو علم ذلك ما أنكر الإعادة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r7.claim: The rotten bones are remains reduced to fragments.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r7.anchor: قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم {78} } [يس: 77-78] رفات

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r8.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r8.claim: Mujāhid reports that Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone and challenged whether God could revive it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r8.anchor: المعلى، عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد، قال: أتى /أبي بن خلف /إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم بال، فقال: أيحيي الله هذا وهو رميم؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r1.claim: The objector has forgotten that God created him; just as God created him once, He will recreate him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r1.anchor: {ونسي خلقه} [يس: 78] وقد علم أنا خلقناه، أي: فكما خلقناه فكذلك نعيده

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports a divine saying: the servant insults God by claiming He has a child and denies Him by saying He will not restore people as He first created them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " قال الله: شتمني عبدي ولم يكن له ليشتمني

ELMALILI:36:77-83/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought a decayed bone to the Prophet, crumbled it, and asked about its revival; the Prophet replied that God would resurrect him too and cast him into the Fire, and this verse was revealed on that occasion.
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r1.anchor: Übey b. Halef Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’in huzûruna bir çürümüş kemikle gelmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.claim: The passage exposes the contradiction of someone who neglects reflection on his own creation, then arrogantly judges the Creator's and Prophet's statements using reason alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.anchor: İnsanın kendi yaratılışı üzerinde düşünmeyi bir kenara bırakıp, küstahça bir tavırla yüce yaratıcının ve peygamberinin bildirdiklerini yalnızca aklıyla

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.claim: If a person accepts the Creator's power to develop a seemingly insignificant drop into an adult, he should not doubt that the same power can revive a decayed bone; pagan Arabs also admitted God created the universe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.anchor: işte bu gücün çürümüş kemiğe de can verebileceğini yadırgamaması gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.claim: Makkan polytheists rejected Muhammad's prophethood and resurrection to preserve the established worship of other gods, and used mockery to influence people around them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.anchor: Resûlullah’ın peygamberliğini ve onun bildirdiklerini, dolayısıyla öldükten sonra dirilme gerçeğini kabul etmemek, sonuç olarak da Allah’ın yanı sıra başka mâbudlara tapma esasına dayalı kurulu düzenlerini sürdürmek için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r5.claim: Reports say a leading polytheist came to the Prophet with a decayed bone, crumbled it, and asked whether God would revive it once pulverized.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r5.anchor: Müşriklerin önde gelenlerinden biri Hz. Peygamber’e elinde çürümüş bir kemik parçasıyla gelir ve onu ufalayıp, “Böyle un ufak olduktan sonra Allah bunu diriltecek öyle mi?” der.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.claim: In the report, the Prophet replies that God will kill the challenger, resurrect him, and cast him into Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem de “Evet. Nitekim O seni de öldürecek, sonra diriltip cehenneme atacak!” cevabını verir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r7.claim: Reports name the interlocutor as Ubayy b. Khalaf, As b. Wa'il, Abu Jahl, or Walid b. al-Mughira; Ibn Ashur suggests similar incidents may have occurred several times.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r7.anchor: Übey b. Halef, Âsî b. Vâil, Ebû Cehil ve Velîd b. Mug^re isimlerinin geçmesi, olayın benzerlerinin birkaç defa meydana gelmiş olması ihtimalini düşündürmektedir (İbn Âşûr

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r8.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya rightly criticizes the report that identifies Abdullah b. Ubayy as the challenger.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r8.anchor: İbn Atıyye, Abdullah b. Übeyy’in adının zikredilmesini haklı olarak eleştirir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r9.claim: The author finds the report most plausible in which Ubayy b. Khalaf, before a group, says he will dispute Muhammad's claim and then brings a decayed bone to the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r9.anchor: “Muhammed Allah’ın ölüleri dirilteceğini söylüyor, bunu onunla tartışacağım!” dedikten sonra çürümüş bir kemik alıp Resûlullah’a gittiği rivayeti daha mâkul görünmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.claim: Razi says the general meaning matters more than the specific occasion: the passage condemns denial of God's power and resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.anchor: Râzî’nin belirttiği üzere önemli olan, özel sebep ne olursa olsun sözün genelinden çıkan mânadır

BURHAN:v4p47/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r2.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p47/r2.claim: Answers normally match the question’s clause type, but Ibn Mālik analyzes a short answer such as ‘Zayd’ to ‘Who read?’ as a verbal clause with its verb omitted; complete answers retain the verb, as in the resurrection exchange.
BURHAN:v4p47/r2.anchor: قال وإنما قدرته كذلك لا مبتدأ مع احتماله

BURHAN:v4p47/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p47/r6.claim: A short answer like ‘Zayd’ explicitly signals that it answers ‘Who came?’; unlike ‘Zayd came,’ it cannot also stand as an unrelated sentence and conveys the restriction ‘the one who came was Zayd.’
BURHAN:v4p47/r6.anchor: ولو قلت زيد كان نصا في أنه جواب وفي العموم الذي دلت عليه من وكأنك قلت الذي جاء زيد فيفيد الحصر

BURHAN:v2p25/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p25/r3.speaker: أبي بن خلف
BURHAN:v2p25/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Khalaf reportedly brought decayed bones, crumbled and scattered them, and challenged Muhammad over who could revive them; the answer points to the first creation and God’s knowledge of every creation.

BURHAN:v3p363/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p363/r1.speaker: البغوي
BURHAN:v3p363/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi explains رميم without ة as shifted from the active participle; words shifted from their source pattern take no ة.
BURHAN:v3p363/r1.anchor: وقال البغوي في قوله تعالى ﴿ من يحيي العظام وهي رميم ﴾ 2 ولم يقل رميمة لأنه معدول عن فاعله

BURHAN:v1p402/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p402/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p402/r1.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from standalone يحيى but retained with its object pronoun: inner life is clearer to knowledge and stronger in perception than outward life.
BURHAN:v1p402/r1.anchor: لأن حياة الباطن أظهر فى العلم من حياة الظاهر وأقوى فى الإدراك

BURHAN:v1p402/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p402/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p402/r3.claim: More generally, omitted yāʾ can signal absence from perception and connection to submission to God in the station of excellence.
BURHAN:v1p402/r3.anchor: الضرب الثانى الذى تسقط فيه الياء فى الخط والتلاوة فهو اعتبار غيبة عن باب الإدراك جملة واتصاله بالإسلام لله

BURHAN:v2p252/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p252/r1.speaker: الحنفية
BURHAN:v2p252/r1.claim: The Hanafis hold that divine takwīn is eternal and subsists in God's essence, while bringing each part of the world into existence when its time comes rather than at the utterance كن.
BURHAN:v2p252/r1.anchor: وقالت الحنفية التكوين ازلي قائم بذات الباري سبحانه وهو تكوين لكل جزء من أجزاء العالم عند وجوده لا أنه يوجد عند كاف ونون

BURHAN:v2p252/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p252/r2.speaker: فخر الإسلام شمس الأئمة
BURHAN:v2p252/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Islam Shams al-Aʾimma says the خطاب كن exists whenever each thing is created, so creation involves both bringing it into existence and the command كن.
BURHAN:v2p252/r2.anchor: وذهب فخر الإسلام شمس الأئمة منهم إلى ان خطاب كن موجود عند إيجاد كل شيء فالحاصل عندهم في ايجاد الشيء شيئان

BURHAN:v2p252/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p252/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p252/r5.claim: The Qur'an contains literal statements that remain on their original sense, including signs of God's existence, oneness, transcendence, and the challenge about reviving decayed bones.
BURHAN:v2p252/r5.anchor: لا خلاف ان كتاب الله يشتمل على الحقائق وهي كل كلام بقي على موضوعه

BURHAN:v3p228/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p228/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p228/r1.claim: The exchange about reviving bones after the denier forgets his own creation is described as the strongest form of argument.
BURHAN:v3p228/r1.anchor: وهذا أشد ما يكون من الحجاج

BURHAN:v3p360/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p360/r11.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p360/r11.claim: Qareeb has the form faʿil, which can agree as masculine or feminine; 36:78 gives a parallel with ramim.
BURHAN:v3p360/r11.anchor: وقيل قريب على وزن فعيل وفعيل يستوي فيها المذكر والمؤنث

ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.claim: Answers generally match the question's sentence form; the verbal answers in 5:4 and 36:79 show that an omitted verb should be estimated before the stated answer.

ITQAN:v4p357/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p357/r3.speaker: أبي بن خلف
ITQAN:v4p357/r3.claim: Al-Hakim and others report that Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbled a bone and challenged whether God could revive it; the verse answered by pointing to first creation.
ITQAN:v4p357/r3.anchor: أن أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم ففته فقال

SULAMI:v2p175#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p175#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p175#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says Quranic parables show sound paths for monotheists and worshippers, teaching that a little of God’s inspiration is better than much of their own practice.
SULAMI:v2p175#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي - رحمة الله عليه - : ضرب الأمثال في القرآن إعلاما لصحة الطرق للموحدين على حدة والعاملين على حدة

SULAMI:v2p175#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p175#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p175#2/r2.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads reviving the dead bones as reviving hearts deadened by hardness and turning away, restoring surrender, trust, and turning toward God.
SULAMI:v2p175#2/r2.anchor: وقال في قوله : ﴿ من يحيي العظام وهي رميم ﴾ أي من يحيي القلوب الميتة بالقسوة والإعراض عنه فيردها إلى التفويض والتسليم والتوكل والإقبال عليه

RUMMANI:v1p106/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r1.claim: Bayān is bringing forward what lets one thing be distinguished from another in perception; it has four forms: speech, a state, a gesture, and a sign.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r1.anchor: البيان هو الإحضار لما يظهر به تميز الشيء من غيره في الإدراك.

RUMMANI:v1p106/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r2.claim: Speech is bayān when it distinguishes a thing through meaning; scrambled or incoherent speech that communicates no sense is not bayān.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r2.anchor: كلام يظهر به تميز الشيء من غيره فهو بيان

RUMMANI:v1p106/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r3.claim: Understandable speech is not automatically good bayān: the rustic's answer about breeding his donkey conveys his meaning but is ugly and faulty in expression.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r3.anchor: كقول السوادي وقد سئل عن أتان معه

RUMMANI:v1p106/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r4.claim: The Baqil anecdote contrasts failed eloquence with successful communication: trying to signal eleven by extending his tongue and ten fingers let the gazelle escape.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r4.anchor: فبلغ من عيه أنه سئل عن ظبية كانت معه

RUMMANI:v1p106/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r6.claim: The highest rank of verbal bayān combines balanced composition, pleasing sound, ease on the tongue, acceptance by the soul, and expression proportionate to the need and its proper status.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r6.anchor: فأعلاها مرتبة ما جمع أسباب الحسن في العبارة من تعديل النظم حتى يحسن في السمع ويسهل على اللسان وتتقبله النفس تقبل البرد

RUMMANI:v1p106/r7.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r7.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r7.claim: Meaning may be conveyed through a noun, an attribute, or composition without either; غلام زيد, for example, conveys ownership through its construction.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r7.anchor: والبيان في الكلام لا يخلو من أن يكون باسم أو صفة أو تأليف

RUMMANI:v1p106/r8.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r8.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r8.claim: Derived forms also imply unstated meanings: قاتل conveys killing and a victim without explicitly naming either, while the possibilities of composition are unlimited.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r8.anchor: ودلالة الاشتقاق كدلالة التأليف في أنه من غير ذكر اسم أو صفة

RUMMANI:v1p106/r9.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r9.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r9.claim: Because names and attributes are finite but compositions have no limit, the Qur'an's challenge by composition reveals its miracle; possible compositions, like numbers, cannot be exhausted, and all Qur'an has consummate bayān.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r9.anchor: ودلالة الأسماء والصفات متناهية , فأما دلالة التأليف فليس لها نهاية

RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.claim: The reply to the denier who forgets his own creation—that the one who created the bones initially will revive them and knows every creation—is singled out as supremely persuasive.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.anchor: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#6/r1.claim: Ramīm means worn away; an old bone is said to have become ramīm or rumām, like rufāt and futāt.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#6/r1.anchor: {وهي رميم} أي بالية. يقال: رم العظم -إذا بلي- فهو رميم ورمام (3) . كما يقال: رفات وفتات.

NAHHAS:v3p406/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p406/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p406/r15.claim: The damma is dropped from yāʾ because it is heavy; assimilation would bring two sukuns together.
NAHHAS:v3p406/r15.anchor: حذفت الضمة من الياء لثقلها ولا يجوز الإدغام لئلا يلتقي ساكنان

SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r1.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r1.claim: One view treats رميم as active participle; missing feminine marking is irregular.
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r1.anchor: قيل: بمعنى فاعل. وقيل: بمعنى مفعول، فعلى الأول عدم التاء غير مقيس.

SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r2.claim: Another view treats رميم as passive participle.
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r2.anchor: وقيل: بمعنى مفعول، فعلى الأول عدم التاء غير مقيس.

SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says رميم is a noun for decayed bones, not adjective or participle.
SAMIN-DURR:36:78/r3.anchor: الرميم اسم لما بلي من العظام غير صفة كالرمة والرفات

ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r1.claim: Asad reads the phrase about coining a simile as an elliptical allusion to deniers' refusal to conceive of a transcendent God beyond sense or imagination, whose powers exceed every created being.
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r1.anchor: Lit., "he coins for Us a simile (mathal)" an elliptic allusion to the unwillingness of "those who deny the truth" to conceive

ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r2.claim: Asad says materialists deny resurrection, thereby denying God's creative power and, ultimately, His existence.
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n46/r2.anchor: Since they are enmeshed in a materialistic outlook on life, such people deny - as the sequence shows - all possibility of resurrection

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r4.claim: Ḍaraba mathalan can mean citing an example or wise saying, or speaking sarcastically and mocking; the mocking sense is intended here.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r4.anchor: Here this latter meaning is implied.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.claim: These verses continue the assurance in verse 76: arrogant Quraysh rival God, forget their creation and mock resurrection, just as they insult the Prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.anchor: These verses are connected to those before them through two aspects: It relates to the assurance sounded to the Prophet (sws) in the previous verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.claim: The earlier account of providence also leads to accountability: God’s favors entail gratitude and monotheism as well as a day of reward and punishment, which people evade.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.anchor: providence entails gratitude and believing in one God, it also entails a day of reward and punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r2.claim: Forgetting one’s creation explains the foolish resurrection question: anyone remembering that God created him from clay would not ask it; asking makes him God’s rival.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r2.anchor: He who remembers that God created him from clay will never ask such a question.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p146#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p146#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p146#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says this was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who scattered a decayed bone in the wind and challenged the Prophet; the Prophet answered that God would revive it, then cause Ubayy to die and enter the Fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p146#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه ﴾ قال نزلت في أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم نخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r9.claim: The objection ‘Who revives the decayed dead?’ is attributed variously to al-ʿĀṣī b. Wāʾil, Umayya b. Khalaf, and Ubayy b. Khalaf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r9.anchor: وقائل ذلك العاصي بن وائل، أو أمية بن خلف، أو أبي بن خلف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r10.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda attribute the resurrection objection to Umayya b. Khalaf; Abū Ḥayyān allows that all three candidates may have made it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r10.anchor: والقول أنه أمية، قاله مجاهد وقتادة ويحتمل أن كلا منهم واقع ذلك منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r11.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r11.claim: Ibn Wahb reports from Mālik that the objector was Ubayy b. Khalaf, also named by Ibn Isḥāq and others; Abū Ḥayyān calls this the strongest view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r11.anchor: أقوال أصحها أنه أبي بن خلف، رواه ابن وهب عن مالك، وقاله ابن إسحاق وغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r12.claim: Ubayy brought a decayed bone in Mecca, crumbled it before the Prophet, and asked who could revive it; the Prophet replied that God would revive it, cause Ubayy to die and live, and enter him into Hell, after which the verse came down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r12.anchor: جاء بالعظم الرميم بمكة، ففتته في وجهه الكريم وقال: من يحيى هذا يا محمد؟ فقال: «الله يحييه ويميتك ويحييك ويدخلك جهنم»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r13.claim: The report adds that the Prophet personally struck Ubayy with a spear at Uḥud, which pierced his neck.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r13.anchor: وأبي هذا قتله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده يوم أحد بالحربة، فخرجت من عنقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r4.claim: He forgets that he originated from a drop, suppressing that fact through stubborn disputation and treating resurrection as impossibly remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r4.anchor: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه: أي نشأته من النطفة، فذهل عنها وترك ذكرها على طريق اللدد والمكابرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r5.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī reads nasiya khāliquhu, ‘he forgot his Creator,’ as an active participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: ونسي خالقه، اسم فاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r6.claim: The majority read khalqahu, meaning that he forgot his own creation or origin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r7.claim: His question about reviving bones is called a parable because it implies a wondrous story, namely denial of God’s power to raise the dead, which humans themselves cannot do.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r7.anchor: وسمى قوله: من يحي العظام وهي رميم لما دل عليه من قصة عجيبة شبيهة بالمثل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats ramīm as a noun for decayed bone, not an adjective, so it needs no feminine ending and is neither an active nor passive participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والرميم اسم لما بلى من العظام غير صفة، كالرمة والرفاة، فلا يقال: لم لم يؤنث؟

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r1.claim: The clause coordinates with the negative clause under one reading, or with the sudden-result clause under the alternative.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r1.anchor: معطوف على حينئذ على الجملة المنفية داخل في حيز الإنكار

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r2.claim: The expression may mean an astonishing story denying resurrection, an absurd fable in his view, or making humans a likeness for God and measuring divine power by human power.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r2.anchor: أي أورد في شأننا قصة عجيبة في نفس الأمر هي في الغرابة كالمثل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r3.claim: He forgot God's creation of him; the phrase may coordinate with the preceding clause or be circumstantial, and forgetting may mean failing to recall, willfully neglecting, or acting as if forgotten.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r3.anchor: أي خلقنا إياه على الوجه المذكور الدال على بطلان ما ضربه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r4.claim: The standalone he said answers an implied question about what parable he offered or what he said.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r4.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال نشأ من حكاية ضربه المثل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r5.claim: He denies anyone could revive bones and highlights their extreme decay by calling them ramim.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r5.anchor: منكرا ذلك ناكرا من أحوال العظام ما تبعد معه من الحياة غاية البعد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r6.claim: Apparently ramim is an adjective, either active from intransitive decay or passive and common to masculine and feminine.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن رميم صفة لا إسم جامد فإن كان من رم اللازم بمعنى بلى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r7.speaker: محي السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r7.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna says ramim lacks feminine marking because it is altered from a feminine form, like baghiy in 19:28 from baghiya.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r7.anchor: محي السنة : لم يقل رميمة لأنه معدول من فاعلة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r8.speaker: الأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r8.claim: Al-Azhari says bones follow a singular pattern like kitab and qirab, so the adjective is singular masculine; al-Alusi calls this unusual.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r8.anchor: الأزهري : إن عظاما لكونه بوزن المفرد ككتاب وقراب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r9.claim: If ramma is transitive, meaning to make decay, ramim is passive; the root evokes eating, so the earth consumed what decayed.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r9.anchor: وإن كان من رم المتعدي بمعنى أبلى يقال رمه أي أبلاه وأصل معناه الأكل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r10.speaker: المطلع
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r10.claim: Al-Mutli' treats ramim as a noun like rimma and rufat, not an adjective; al-Alusi doubts this because it has a verb and adjectival pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54/r10.anchor: وفي المطلع الرميم اسم غير صفة كالرمة والرفات لا فعيل بمعنى فاعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r1.claim: “He forgot his creation” means that he forgot how his own origin began.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r1.anchor: نسي خلقه} بدء أمره، ثم {قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} بالية،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r2.claim: Ramim means worn and decayed; the form is used instead of feminine ramimah because it is diverted from its usual feminine pattern.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r2.anchor: {قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} بالية، ولم يقل رميمة؛ لأنه معدول عن فاعلة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r3.claim: Forms diverted from their usual form do not follow their ordinary counterparts; Maryam 19:28 similarly has baghiy without the feminine ending because it is diverted from baghiyah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r3.anchor: عن وجهه ووزنه كان مصروفا عن أخواته (1) ، كقوله: "وما كانت أمك بغيا"

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.claim: The man advances an astonishing claim denying the power to resurrect the dead, or compares resurrection with what humans cannot do and describes God as unable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.anchor: أمرا عجيبا وهو نفي القدرة على إحياء الموتى

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r2.claim: He forgets that God created him in the first place.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r3.claim: Ramīm means decayed bones; the form may be active or passive participle, and it lacks feminine marking because it became a fixed noun.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.claim: The verse indicates that bones possess life and are affected by death like the other bodily members.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن العظم ذو حياة فيؤثر فيه الموت كسائر الأعضاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r7.speaker: أبي بن خلف الجمحي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r7.claim: The occasion was Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, whom the Prophet killed in single combat at Uhud; he is the primary target of this rebuke.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r7.anchor: وسبب النزول أبي بن خلف الجمحي الذي قتله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأحد مبارزة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r8.claim: The opponent makes the powerless idols he worships a comparison for God, despite reason showing that nothing resembles the Creator and idols can do nothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r8.anchor: أي آلهته التي عبدها لكونها لا تقدر على شيء مكابرا لعقله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r9.claim: Nasiya khalqahu can mean that he became heedless of his creation or that he abandoned reflection on it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r9.anchor: والنسيان هنا يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى الذهول , وأن بكون بمعنى الترك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r10.claim: The analogy is so foolish that it would not satisfy even a donkey if one could speak, rebuking the opponent's obtuseness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r10.anchor: هذا المثل الذب قاله هذا الكافر لا يرضاه حمار لو نطق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r11.claim: The question treats reviving the dead as impossible; bones are the hardest matter and least receptive to life, especially once decayed and crumbled.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r11.anchor: ولما كانت العظام أصلب شيء وأبعده عن قبول الحياة لا سيما إذا بليت وأرفتت

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r12.claim: Ramīm means the bones have become dust that is carried along by the wind.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r12.anchor: أي صارت ترابا يمر مع الرياح

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the objector as Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crumbled a bone and asked whether people would be revived after becoming like that decayed bone.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : وضرب لنا مثلا قال : أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202#2/r1.claim: ʿIkrima reports that Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a withered bone and asked whether God would revive it; the verse was revealed, and Muhammad replied that God had already created it once.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله ، عنه قال : جاء أبي بن خلف إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي يده عظم حائل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Hasan identify the man who brought the decayed bone as Umayya ibn Khalaf; al-Rummani records al-Hasan's report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: إن الذي جاء بالعظم النخر أمية بن خلف، وقاله الحسن ذكره الرماني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to identify the man who brought the bone as Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الجائي بالعظم هو عبد الله بن أبي ابن سلول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r4.claim: The attribution to Ibn Abbas is mistaken: the sura and verse are Meccan by consensus, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy never made such an open challenge; confusion over the name Ubayy misled transmitters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r4.anchor: وهو وهم ممن نسبه إلى ابن عباس لأن السورة والآية مكية بإجماع ولأن عبد الله بن أبي لم يجاهر قط هذه المجاهرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r5.claim: The sound account, transmitted by Ibn Wahb from Malik and also stated by Ibn Ishaq and others, is that Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Umayya's brother, brought and crumbled the bone in Mecca before the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r5.anchor: لأن الصحيح هو ما رواه ابن وهب عن مالك، وقاله ابن إسحاق وغيره، من أن أبي بن خلف أخا أمية بن خلف هو الذي جاء بالعظم الرميم بمكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet replied to Ubayy that God would revive the bone, cause Ubayy to die and be raised, and admit him to Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r6.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي حين فت العظم «الله يحييه ويميتك ويحييك ويدخلك جهنم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r8.claim: نسي may mean forgetfulness or deliberate neglect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r8.anchor: وقوله ونسي يحتمل أن يكون نسيان الذهول ويحتمل أن يكون نسيان الترك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r9.claim: رميم means worn away and crumbled, that is, reduced to remains.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r1.claim: The unbeliever argues against resurrection by crushing a decayed bone and expressing astonishment that anyone says God will revive it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r1.anchor: في إنكار البعث بالعظم البالي حين فته بيده وتعجب ممن يقول إن الله يحييه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r2.claim: Forgetting his creation means neglecting to consider how God created him from a drop.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r2.anchor: أي نسي خلقنا له أي ترك النظر في خلق نفسه إذ خلق من نطفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r3.claim: Ramīm means decayed or crumbled; the verb ramma is used of a bone becoming worn away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r3.anchor: أي بالية يقال رم العظم إذا بلي فهو رميم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r4.claim: Ramīm has been shifted from its expected active-participle form; forms shifted from their regular pattern are declined unusually.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r4.anchor: لأنه معدول عن فاعله وكل معدول عن وجهه و وزنه فهو مصروف عن إعرابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi compares the shifted form with Maryam 19:28, where the final feminine tāʾ is omitted from baghiy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r5.anchor: مريم 28 فأسقط الهاء لأنها مصروفة عن باغية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r6.claim: The unbeliever wrongly measures God's power by human capacity and denies revival because people cannot revive decayed bones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p41/r6.anchor: فقاس هذا الكافر قدرة الله تعالى بقدرة الخلق فأنكر إحياء العظم البالي لأن ذلك ليس في مقدور الخلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد، وعكرمة، وعروة بن الزبير، والسدي، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.claim: These authorities report that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to Muhammad with a decayed bone, crumbled and scattered it, and challenged whether God would resurrect it; the final verses of Yasin were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وعروة بن الزبير، والسدي. وقتادة: جاء أبي بن خلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says al-Asi ibn Waʾil took a bone from al-Batha, crushed it, and asked Muhammad whether God could revive it; Muhammad said God would resurrect and send him to Hell, and Yasin's closing verses were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير (6) ، عن ابن عباس، أن العاصي (7) بن وائل أخذ عظما من البطحاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits the al-Asi ibn Waʾil report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr but does not name Ibn Abbas in its chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.anchor: ورواه ابن جرير عن يعقوب بن إبراهيم، عن هشيم، عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، فذكره ولم يذكر "ابن عباس"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.claim: Al-Awfi's report names Abdullah ibn Ubayy as the visitor, but Ibn Kathir rejects it as munkar because Yasin is Meccan and Ibn Ubayy was in Medina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.anchor: وروي من طريق العوفي، عن ابن عباس قال: جاء عبد الله بن أبي بعظم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r3.claim: The denier mocks resurrection as impossible for the Creator of heaven and earth, yet forgets that God created him from nothing, something more astonishing than what he rejects.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r3.anchor: ونسي نفسه، وأن الله خلقه من العدم، فعلم من نفسه ما هو أعظم مما استبعده وأنكره وجحده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.speaker: حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.claim: Ahmad reports Hudhayfa's account of a dying man who ordered his family to burn and scatter his remains; God reassembled and questioned him, then forgave him for fearing God. Uqba ibn Amr confirms hearing the Prophet tell it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.anchor: عن ربعي قال: قال عقبة بن عمرو لحذيفة: ألا تحدثنا ما سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r8.claim: One grammatical explanation treats ramīm as shifted away from its normal agent form, which permits altered inflection and gender.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r8.anchor: قيل: (رميم) ولم يقل: رميمة؛ لأنه معدول عن فاعله، وما كان معدولا عن وجهه ووزنه

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r9.claim: Another explanation allows masculine ramīm because the bones’ femininity is not biologically real.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r9.anchor: وقيل: تأنيث العظام ليس بحقيقي، فجاز تذكيره

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.claim: A polytheist brought a crumbled old bone and challenged Muhammad about God reviving it; the passage from this verse to the sūra’s end was revealed.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.anchor: قيل: جاء مشرك بعظم بال متفتت، وقال: يا محمد، أتزعم أن الله يبعث هذا بعدما بلي؟ فقال: نعم، فنزلت الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.speaker: أبي بن خلف
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf, with Abu Jahl, al-Asi ibn Wa'il, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, challenged Muhammad by crushing a decayed bone; the Prophet answered that God would revive him and cast him into Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.anchor: فقال لهم أبي : ألا ترون إلى ما يقول محمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r3.claim: Calling the objection a مثل either marks its strange, striking story of denying resurrection or its implied comparison about what God can do.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r3.anchor: لما دل عليه من قصة عجيبة شبيهة بالمثل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r4.claim: Denying God's ability to do what His first creation proves He can do amounts to challenging Him and likening Him to creatures unable to revive the dead.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r4.anchor: كان تعجيزا لله وتشبيها له بخلقه في أنهم غير موصوفين بالقدرة عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r5.claim: رميم is a noun for crumbled bones, like رمة and رفات, not an adjective; it needs no feminine agreement and is neither an active nor passive participle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r5.anchor: والرميم : اسم لما بلي من العظام غير صفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r6.claim: Those who hold that bones contain life cite this verse to argue dead bones are impure because death affects them after life inhabits them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r6.anchor: ولقد استشهد بهذه الآية من يثبت الحياة في العظام ويقول : إن عظام الميتة نجسة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r7.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa's school considers bones, sinews, and nerves pure because life does not inhabit them; they take reviving bones to mean restoring them fresh and moist in a living body.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r7.anchor: وأما أصحاب أبي حنيفة فهي عندهم طاهرة ، وكذلك الشعب والعصب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports al-As ibn Wa'il crumbling a bone and questioning resurrection; the Prophet said God would revive him, then kill and resurrect him and put him in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآيات فيه ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r6.claim: Forgetting creation may mean failing to use it as evidence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, it means forgetting to reflect on his creation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r8.claim: His question expresses disbelief that decayed bones could be made anew.

MUQATIL:36:76-78/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r4.claim: Ubayy likened God's power to a bone, forgetting that he himself began as a drop and once did not exist, then asked who could revive decayed bones.
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r4.anchor: { وضرب لنا مثلا } وصف لنا شبها فى أمر العظم { ونسي خلقه } وترك المنظر فى بدء خلق نفسه إذ خلق من نطفة

MUQATIL:36:76-78/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r5.anchor: { قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم } [آية: 78] يعنى بالية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r1.claim: The objector made his example by crumbling a bone.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r2.claim: He forgot that God first created him from semen, a more remarkable origin than reviving bone.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r2.anchor: من المنى فهو أغرب من إحياء العظم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r3.claim: The verbal noun is annexed to its object: God created him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r3.anchor: المصدر مضاف إلى المفعول أى خلقنا إياه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r4.claim: Ramīm is a noun for decayed bones rather than an adjective such as ramma or rufāt.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r4.anchor: هو اسم لما بلى من العظام غير صفة كالرمة والرفات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r5.claim: Because ramīm is a noun it is not made feminine, though it is predicated of the feminine noun bones.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r5.anchor: ولهذا لم يؤنث وقد وقع خبر المؤنث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r6.claim: Some who say life inhabits bones and death makes carrion bones impure cite this verse; Nasafi holds bones, hair, and sinews pure because life does not inhabit them and death does not affect them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r6.anchor: ومن يثبت الحياة فى العظام ويقول إن عظام الميتة نجسة لأن الموت يؤثر فيها من قبل أن الحياة تحلها يتشبث بهذه الآية وهى عندنا طاهرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r7.claim: Reviving the bones means restoring them to their former fresh, moist state within a living, sensing body.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15/r7.anchor: والمراد باحياء العظام فى الآية ردها إلى ما كانت عليه غضة رطبة فى بدن حى حساس

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.claim: The denier forgot that God first made him from a lifeless drop and assembled life in him.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r1.anchor: أي ونسي أنا أنشأناه من نطفة ميتة فركبنا فيه الحياة

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r4.claim: Ramīm means decayed; the bone is called ramīm or ramām when it has crumbled away.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.claim: Ramīm is masculine because it is shifted from the feminine fāʿila form; likewise بغيا drops its feminine ending as shifted from باغية.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.anchor: وإنما قال رميم ولم يقل رميمة لأنها معدولة عن فاعلة

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة وبعض أصحاب الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa and some Shafiʿi associates hold that bones have life and become impure at death.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r10.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة وبعض أصحاب الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r11.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r11.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that bones have no life, differing from Abu Hanifa and some of his own associates.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r11.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه: لا حياة فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r12.claim: The suggestion that bones means their owners by an omitted possessive is unnecessary; no ellipsis is needed here.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r12.anchor: قلنا: إنما يكون إذا احتيج لضرورة وليس هاهنا ضرورة تدعو إلى هذا الإضمار

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r13.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r13.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says sensory perception, a sign of life, is present in bones, supporting the literal reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r13.anchor: فإن الإحساس الذي هو علامة الحياة موجود فيه قاله ابن العربي
